items.title: Pretend you're sitting at Elizabeth Holmes' desk on this weirdly detailed website
items.snippet: With over a thousand emails, slides, texts, and documents unveiled during the United States v. Elizabeth Holmes trial, Extend engineer Bo Lau created a website that simulates what it might have been like to be the chief executive of Theranos before everything came crashing down. (Every day, I am grateful to the American legal system for making the discovery process public.) i built a website where you can sit at elizabeth holmes’ desk open her macbook, scroll her iphone, run the theranos edison machine her texts, emails, slides, documents, and theranos machine records are real, sourced from exhibits in the united states v. holmes criminal trial pic.twitter.com/5At9T5m3UV The environment that Lau created is ambitiously detailed, taking you right back to 2016, a time when iPhones had home buttons, and you had to slide your finger across the screen to unlock it. Even the MacBook Air is running OS X El Capitan. You can click around the environment, which lets you look through the documents made public from the court case on Holmes’ iPhone and laptop screens. You can even run the Therano…

items.title: Fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute misconduct claims, warn of chilling effect

items.title: Ben Affleck is an AI nerd, and the internet is impressed
items.snippet: They cast the wrong lead in “Good Will Hunting,” apparently, because it’s Ben Affleck who is the secret genius, as it turns out. The actor who earlier this year sold his AI filmmaking startup to Netflix for a reported $587 million has gone viral this week for demonstrating his understanding of AI technology, neural networks, machine learning, and the like, across multiple video clips of his recent interviews. The movie star delved into his interest in technology most recently on an episode of GQ’s “One More Question” series this week, where he humbly started with “I’ve always been kind of into computers since I was young,” before nerding out on the development of AI as it relates to filmmaking, while using AI terminology like machine learning, neural networks, transformers, tensors, GPUs, inference, and more. In a clip that’s making the rounds, Affleck explains to the impressed interviewer, Zach Baron, that he got into the space when analog film moved to digital. items.title: Popular AI leaderboard Arena nearly doubles valuation to $3.1B valuation in 10 months
items.snippet: The company behind the popular LMArena leaderboard has raised $200 million led by Lightspeed and Khosla, and is now measuring AI models on alignment issues such as lying.

items.title: OpenAI's revenue is reportedly $20 billion less than previously projected
items.snippet: It had previously been reported that the AI lab's annualized revenue was some $70 billion, but a new report claims it's a whole lot less than that.

items.title: Google brings agentic AI to Gemini, starting with businesses
items.snippet: Google is turning Gemini into an AI agent that can plan, execute tasks, and work across business apps and systems. The agent can delegate work to subagents, use multiple AI models, and even gets its own workplace identity, complete with an email address.

items.title: Anthropic changes usage policy to ban model abuse and election interference
items.snippet: Anthropic's updated usage policy explicitly prohibits users from repeatedly abusing Claude in extreme cases, though ordinary frustration and criticism are still allowed. The new rules also address election interference, deceptive campaigns, weapons software, and surveillance.

items.title: OpenAI's math solutions aren't meeting the field's standards yet
items.snippet: OpenAI's flood of proofs deviated from the guidelines set by a group of mathematical researchers consulted by the frontier lab.

items.title: A startup founder who served time in prison is looking to court an untapped market: ex-cons
items.snippet: Richard Bronson, a former Stratton Oakmont partner who served time in federal prison for securities violations, has launched Commissary Club, a startup that uses AI to help people leaving prison find jobs, housing, community, and even dates.

items.title: Natura’s $99 smart ring puts AI agents on your finger
items.snippet: Natura’s $99 Interface smart ring lets you summon AI agents with the press of a finger to complete tasks, capture thoughts, and control devices — while doubling as a health tracker.

items.title: Goodfire says its new ‘inside-out’ monitors catch rogue AI agents at a fraction of the cost
items.snippet: Goodfire just launched what it says is a cheaper way to keep AI agents in check: Instead of paying a second AI to read everything an agent does, its monitors peek inside the model while it works and only call in backup when something looks fishy.

items.title: US bars Microsoft, Adobe, and major IT firms from green card program for skilled foreign workers
items.snippet: The other firms being suspended from the program include Capgemini, Cognizant, HCL, Infosys, Tata, and Wipro.

items.title: Elon Musk questions Ambani’s influence as Starlink India launch stalls
items.snippet: “Is Ambani the real boss of India?” Elon Musk asked as he questioned why Starlink has yet to launch its satellite internet service in the country.

items.title: New York alleges TikTok gave teens, children a placebo safety feature instead of a real one
items.snippet: New York’s lawsuit against the company is one of more than two dozen cases brought by states accusing the social media giant of designing its platform to encourage addictive use among children.

items.snippet: CEO John Ternus is making changes to Apple's leadership, reports Bloomberg . Apple veteran Steve Smith will take over mergers and acquisitions and corporate development, which was previously led by Adrian Perica. items.title: Apple accuses OpenAI of improperly adding new arguments to trade secrets case
items.snippet: A few days ago, OpenAI accused Apple of improperly adding new evidence to its trade secrets case. Today, Apple fired back with its own accusation that OpenAI went beyond what court rules permit in its response. Here are the details. One of the many aspects of the lawsuit in which Apple accuses two former employees (Chang Liu and Tang Tan), OpenAI, and io Products of trade secret misappropriation involves a request for a preliminary injunction. In a nutshell, Apple has asked the court to issue a preliminary injunction, arguing that it would prevent its trade secrets from becoming further embedded in OpenAI’s hardware development while the case plays out. As part of the legal back-and-forth over that request, Apple filed a reply brief supported by five expert declarations. That, in turn, led the defendants to accuse Apple of improperly introducing new evidence and ask the court to disregard some of the material. items.title: Today in Apple history: Michael Dell says he'd shut down Apple
items.snippet: October 6, 1997: Michael Dell makes an incredibly bleak appraisal of Apple’s fortunes, uttering a quote that will become notorious. Asked what he would do with the struggling company, the founder of Dell Inc. says he would “shut it down and give the money back to the shareholders.” As incorrect forecasts go, this ultimately will go down as one of the more notable in tech history. But it doesn’t seem that way at the time. Sometimes even the tech industry’s smartest people prove spectacularly bad at seeing what comes next. In 1997, Michael Dell had plenty of reason to think Apple was finished. The company was hemorrhaging money, its product strategy was an utter mess, and Apple co-founder Steve Jobs had just returned to the company he’d been forced out of a decade and a half before. What Dell didn’t know was that Apple was standing at the edge of one of the greatest turnarounds in business history — and his throwaway remark would become a perfect reminder that even industry giants can mistake a company’s darkest moment for its final chapter. They can carry astonishing amounts of data, drive high-resolution displays, and deliver serious amounts of power—but generally only when the thing at the other end is close by. But imagine the possibilities if the cable was really, really long. OWC’s new USB4 40Gb/s Active Optical Cables come in 9.8-foot (3 meters) and 16.4-foot (5-meter) lengths, with the latter stretching to about the length as a two-person canoe or an adult saltwater crocodile (pro tip: never mix those two together). items.title: Apple’s ‘lighter’ touchscreen MacBook Pro might not be much thinner after all
items.snippet: Macworld Apple’s imminent MacBook Pro launch offers plenty of reasons to be excited, not least the fact that it’s expected to feature an OLED touchscreen display: the first on an Apple laptop. But one of the other rumored upgrades no longer appears to be on the menu. Having predicted on multiple occasions that the touchscreen MacBook Pro would be thinner than current models, well-connected leaker Mark Gurman has this week played down that aspect of the redesign. items.title: Best Thunderbolt and USB-C docking stations for your MacBook 2026
items.snippet: Macworld Plug your MacBook in and out of a multi-port laptop docking station to swiftly add multiple devices and external displays with just one cable connection to your laptop. We tested the top contenders to find the best Thunderbolt and USB-C docks available to owners of the MacBook Air and MacBook Pro. MacBook Neo users can use any of these docks but are limited to a 10Gbps bandwidth and some display limitations. Thunderbolt, USB4 or USB-C The connectors all look the same (technically known as a “Type-C connector”), but there are significant differences, particularly on speed that will determine both data-transfer rate and higher external display refresh rates. items.title: Surface Laptop Ultra is Microsoft’s best effort to catch up to Apple
items.snippet: Macworld On Wednesday, Microsoft introduced the Surface Laptop Ultra , the first laptop to ship with Nvidia’s new RTX Spark processor (there will be offerings from other companies like HP and Lenovo, too). At a glance, it seems pretty clear that they’re gunning for Apple. Up to 20 ARM-based CPU cores and a big fat Nvidia Blackwell GPU with up to 6,144 cores (Nvidia and Apple count GPU cores very differently). A big bright HDR display, from 24GB to 128GB of RAM, and SSDs from 512GB to 2TB… this is Microsoft’s version of a MacBook Pro, all right. items.title: New HomePod rumors: HomePod mini 2, HomePad and touchscreen HomePod
items.snippet: Macworld Apple’s HomePod lineup could be about to undergo its biggest expansion since the original HomePod launched. Apple is reportedly preparing a new HomePod mini and smart home display for October 13 , with another full-size HomePod expected further down the line, as it builds a new generation of home products around Siri AI. For much of 2025 and 2026, Apple’s revamped Siri was the thing holding those products back. items.title: Apple Watch Series 12 & Ultra 4: Everything you need to know about the 2026 Apple Watches
items.snippet: Macworld In September 2026 Apple unveiled the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 , with both models focusing much more heavily on health monitoring, Apple Intelligence and battery efficiency than on physical redesigns. Series 12 remains Apple’s mainstream premium smartwatch, while Ultra 4 continues as the larger, tougher model aimed at endurance sports, outdoor activities and diving. Both Apple Watches went on sale on September 18. items.title: M6 deep dive: Brilliant 2nm design, but short on bandwidth
items.snippet: Macworld Our own review of the new Mac mini analyzed the performance and value of the M5 Pro version, but that chip has been around since the spring. Far more interesting is the M6, a new-generation processor made on TSMC’s 2nm process and sporting some interesting architectural changes. Our German sister site Macwelt reviewed that model , and found it to be a big jump over the preview Mac mini, which came equipped with an M4. items.title: Atlassian’s critical flaw turns eight enterprise products into one big security problem
items.snippet: A newly-disclosed critical flaw in Atlassian’s data center software has a remarkably wide reach, affecting eight core products across the company’s enterprise portfolio. CVE-2026-21589 , rated 9.3 (critical) in severity, is an arbitrary file access vulnerability that could allow an attacker with no login access to read files in web app root directories that they should not otherwise see, and potentially use them for nefarious purposes. The impacted products require “immediate attention,” Atlassian said in a security advisory . Customers should patch to the latest fixed versions. The company said it has not yet found evidence of exploitation in its cloud offerings, which are already patched.

items.title: Nvidia-backed Upscale takes on AI networking silos with Token Fabric
items.snippet: AI clusters depend on two types of networking. Scale-up networking connects accelerators inside a rack. Scale-out networking connects racks across the data center. Networking startup Upscale today introduced Token Fabric to bring the two together. The architecture combines the company’s own SkyFabriX scale-up silicon, scale-out systems built on Nvidia Spectrum-X Ethernet, and a common software layer for operations.
